correctness.rationale: The line-usage counting is forced because each selected vertex has exactly one selected neighbor, and all components are pairwise line-disjoint dominoes. At most one row and at most one column may be missing, and they may not both be missing. A missing row forces every domino vertical via the duplicated-singleton signature obstruction, yielding a=2b+1; symmetry gives the other exceptional case. When no line is missing, linear row/column equations give the three-divisibility condition and h,v. The converse establishes distinctness among all selected and unselected signatures, including potential swapped row-column decompositions. Labeled block matching counts exactly once and gives the EGF. Direct adjacency enumeration checks all 20 rectangles in check_output.txt, but is explicitly not the infinite proof. Boundary a=b=1 yields no code.

originality.rationale: The source-defining 2017 and 2021/2022 articles were inspected at their relevant theorems and graph-family discussions: neither establishes a full rook-graph dimension criterion, all-set domino classification, factorial census, or bivariate EGF. Studer et al. (2000) require only induced matching and ordinary domination, not pairwise distinct open signatures. Targeted synonym searches disclosed no implication covering the theorem. This is best-knowledge originality, not a proof of world-wide priority. A previously available rook-graph dissociation-polynomial formula already enumerates all line-disjoint domino components and supplies the factorial component weights. The present factorial factors can be recovered from that formula after the additional open-signature admissibility criterion is proved, and are not claimed as independent from that combinatorial census. The genuinely different assertion is the exact open-independent locating predicate on the dissociation profiles, with its sharp absent and boundary cases.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently phrased earlier work may already classify open-independent locating codes on K_a square K_b or L(K_{a,b}).

The 2000 induced-paired domination scan inspected the relevant abstract/early material, not every scanned page; no decisive same-parameter coverage was suggested by its stated problem or section roadmap.
No search result or database partition can establish absolute research priority.

The factorial profile weights are already available in a broader dissociation count; the novelty claim rests on the newly proved nonempty-and-distinct open-signature criterion and sharply characterized admissible profiles, not on independent discovery of these counting weights.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural-family classification of a location-detection invariant whose general existence problem is computationally hard. It gives a surprising dimension-modulo-three/nonmonotone existence pattern, rigid solution size, sharp one-unused-line exceptions, exact factorial counts and a bivariate exponential species enumerator. These facts are not routine relabelings or known scalar parameter substitutions and may inform other line-graph locating-code calculations. The natural rook graph/line graph of a biclique motivates every dimension and coefficient. The factorial factors themselves may be obtained from an existing rook dissociation enumeration, but that general counting result does not give the open-signature selection rule, the existence criterion, or the two exceptional ratios.
